newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 24.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on October 24. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

It would not be in Indonesia's interests for PT Astra International, the country's largest car manufacturer, to fall under the control of one single shareholder, State Secretary Murdiono said. Astra has recently been the focus of heavy trading on the Jakarta Stock Exchange.

Indonesia's Legal Aid Institute (LBH) has said that the responsibility for the death of a man charged with robbery must lie with the police because he was in their custody. The LBH called for a full investigation into the incident.

The government will review its local laws on alcohol in 15 of Indonesia's provinces. The application of the law in Jakarta recently caused outroar among some Moslem scholars who said the government was moving to condone the consumption of alcohol.

Colombian President Ernesto Samper met President Suharto on Wednesday for talks. Suharto said that the two countries had had a good relationship working within the framework of the 118-member Non-Aligned Movement, of which Colombia is currently president.
Timber tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan has bought around a five percent stake in car manufacturer PT Astra Internasional, financial market sources said.
